items.title: Row over plan for ferry terminal at Perth's Matilda Bay deepens

image.altText: An artist's impression of the proposed Matilda Bay ferry terminal in Perth, viewed from the shore.

children.content: A WA government-commissioned analysis finds the scenic and popular Matilda Bay is the safest spot for a ferry terminal, just as another report prompted by an advocacy group says it would put river users at serious risk.

items.title: Lack of volunteers sees Pride events cancelled in regional WA

children.content: In the remote WA town of Carnarvon, Queernavon has been running pride events for three years. A lack of volunteers means they may not go ahead this year and organisers worry about what that will mean for the community.

image.altText: Woman cheering waving rainbow flag above her head in Pride parade.

items.title: Fitzroy Crossing calls for stronger FASD support

children.content: Aboriginal leaders in WA's north have urged the state government to provide more support for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.

image.altText: Three school children together during FASD Awareness march in Fitzroy Crossing.

items.title: Minister flies to Pilbara after report of up to 15 kids living unsupervised

children.content: Child Protection Minister Jessica Stojkovski flies into Port Hedland amid a report that up to 15 children, some as young as five, are living unsupervised in a home in South Hedland.

image.altText: A WA Government jet sits on the tarmac at Port Hedland Airport.

children.content: Almost 70 per cent of public housing tenants in Western Australia's remote Kimberley region are waiting on urgent repairs, research has found.

items.title: Surfer rushed to hospital after shark attack in WA's Midwest

image.altText: The man's surfboard removed from the beach after the attack.

children.content: Authorities say the man is in a "serious but stable" condition after he was bitten by a shark while surfing north of Geraldton.

items.title: ASX drops, Saudi Arabia's shutdown of critical pipeline pushes oil higher

children.content: The ASX is trading lower after Wall Street finished in the red. Oil prices rose sharply after Saudi Arabia shut down its key East-West pipeline which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: One Nation MP leaves door open to slashing citizens' family visas

children.content: One Nation MP David Farley says he is open to cutting visas for family members of Australian citizens, after the party announces a policy to stop temporary skilled migrants bringing their spouses and children to the country.

items.title: Designer to the stars Bob Mackie dies at 87

children.content: Dubbed the Designer to the Stars, Bob Mackie won nine Emmy Awards and a Tony Award, and was nominated for three Oscars, including one for Barbra Streisand's Funny Lady, in which she wore a sheer bat-wing gown.

image.altText: Cher, left, in a black and white jacket and matching hat, and designer Bob Mackie.

items.title: New social rental apartment building in Perth CBD underway

children.content: The building will include 174 one- and two-bedroom rentals, 139 of which will be used for affordable housing, with the rest for social housing, according to the government.

items.title: WorkSafe investigates shovel fire at Kalgoorlie Super Pit

children.content: WorkSafe WA is investigating a workplace incident at one of Australia's biggest gold mines, where the operator of a heavy-duty $18 million mining shovel escaped a fire that engulfed the driver's cab.

image.altText: A large mining shovel badly damaged by fire.
